name: Meridian Water Taxi
description: Small motorized boats operating as taxi services along the lakefront and harbor channels. Licensed operators run fiberglass hulls with electric outboards, seating 4-6 passengers. Unlicensed operators run anything that floats. The water taxi network fills the gaps the ferry system doesn't cover — late night runs, off-schedule trips, routes to the smaller docks and platforms that dot the harbor. In winter, ice boats and hovercraft take over.
cost: Φ5-15 per trip depending on distance and desperation
armament: None. Flare gun. The lake handles disputes.
common_usage: Harbor transit, late-night lakefront travel, reaching island platforms, fishing community transport.
story_hooks: A water taxi operator finds a passenger floating in the lake and picks them up — they have no memory and no identity
Water taxis are disappearing in a specific area of the harbor at night, returning empty hours later with the engines still running
physical_description: Weathered fiberglass hulls, 18-24 feet long, painted faded blues and grays with chipped corporate logos or hand-stenciled operator names. Electric outboards hum quietly, their casings corroded by salt spray and industrial runoff. Vinyl bench seating shows water stains and duct-tape repairs; older unlicensed rigs sport salvaged seats from decommissioned vehicles, oil-stained canvas canopies, and visible jury-rigged wiring running along the gunwales.
